final.question: "Eleven years a nurse. The person who asks why the system makes the safe thing the slow thing."
final.form: The Plan–Do–Study–Act audit cycle, but only inside the two case studies; the page-level parts (Opening, The why, The role, two case studies, Dashboards, Teaching, Close) are the usual portfolio sections renamed.
final.object: The colour-banded Early Warning Score trend line running the full length of the page as its spine — idling green, peaking red at the near-miss, forking into six at the ward rollout, narrowing as scanning climbs, settling at rest.

swap.reason: The spine's beats are keyed to her own two projects — the fork into six lines for her sheet's rollout, the band narrowing with the scanning climb, the 28-cell bed grid — not to nursing in general.

backdrop.reason: The EWS line is the page's organising structure and encodes the argument (deterioration caught early, spread to six wards, variability reduced); deleting it would leave a conventional text page.

depth.reason: It runs cause to consequence — the near-miss, the role it created, the two pieces of work it produced, then the bookended calm and the ask — and the order cannot be shuffled.

clipart.reason: The agent deliberately dropped the stock ECG squiggle for the hand-charted EWS trend chart, an insider working document rather than the public emblem of the job.

honesty.reason: The final plan credits pharmacy, IT and night staff for 71→94, names her paper titles, keeps the whiteboard photo and all identifying detail off the site, and uses no logo.

thirty_seconds.reason: Name and correct title line sit in the hero, her name and a CV tag persist in the corner on every section, and the progress rail lets a visitor jump straight to the contact block.

plain_reader.reason: "Eleven years a nurse. The person who asks why the system makes the safe thing the slow thing" is plain enough for a recruiter and pointed enough for a clinician.

judgement.summary: A single-scroll site spined by an Early Warning Score trend line, with two case studies (the ISBAR handover sheet, the barcode-scanning study) structured as Plan–Do–Study–Act loops and only two modelled objects — fanned blank sheets and a wristband under a scanner beam — plus a dark/light night-and-day register, correct titles, no logo and no identifying detail. Its weakest points are that the first reply had already planned the bed-14/warfarin details and alt text for the whiteboard photo as site content before any clearance, and that the final page still has no question put to the visitor and answered — its top-level parts are the standard hero/about/projects/skills/contact sequence in clinical dress, and the reply twice claims to have saved the plan to memory although no file was written.
